name: D360 Bank
legal_name: D360 Bank (Closed Joint Stock Company, CR 1010822737)
founded: Licensed by Council of Ministers decree no. 389 of 15 Feb 2022 (initial capital SAR 1.65bn, led by Derayah Financial); Derayah says it incubated D360 from 2018; early services for a customer waitlist from Nov 2023; SAMA no-objection to launch banking operations announced 18 Dec 2024, commercial launch Dec 2024.
ownership_summary: Unlisted closed joint-stock company with SAR 2.1bn paid-up capital (website footer, checked 12 Oct 2026). Named main investors are the Public Investment Fund (PIF) and Derayah Financial (Tadawul-listed), which held 20.4% at 31 Mar 2026. Shareholders approved a SAR 1.5bn capital increase in Jun 2026 (72.9m new shares at SAR 20.57; SAR 4.5bn pre-money, SAR 6bn post-money valuation), after which Derayah expects about 16.35%. PIF's percentage and other shareholders are not disclosed in the sources found.

shareholders.holder: Public Investment Fund (PIF): named as a main investor on D360's About page; percentage not disclosed

government_link: Yes: the Public Investment Fund (Saudi sovereign wealth fund) is a named main investor, stake not disclosed (S1, S13). Licensed by Cabinet decree and supervised by SAMA. Checked 2026-10-12.
group_structure: Standalone bank, not consolidated by any shareholder: Derayah accounts for its stake under the equity method (S6, S8). Derayah is described as having appointed more than 30% of D360's board members and treats the bank as a related party (Al Arabiya summary of Derayah's Tadawul filing, S24, search results only). A SAR 1.5bn capital increase approved in Jun 2026 is part of a Series A round that began in 2025 (S12); an employee share programme of 8.75m shares is planned (S24).
footprint: Saudi Arabia only; digital-only (app and web, no branches found). Registered office 7913 King Abdulaziz Rd, Al Arid district, Riyadh (S1). Checked 2026-10-12.
customer_segments: Retail (young families, SME employees, expats, students), SMEs (freelancers, micro SMEs, one-person businesses, SMEs) and API-based banking clients (tech and e-commerce companies, fintechs and non-bank financial institutions, startups), per Derayah's description (S7). Personal financing is open to Saudi nationals only (S4).
business_lines: Retail: current account with travel-oriented debit card (no international fees), Masareef prepaid card for family spending, Ehsan donation card, Pink card, Sanabil Monthly and Daily savings accounts, personal financing (SAR 5,000 to 1,000,000, up to 5 years), international transfers and MoneyGram, Musaned payments, Apple Pay, Samsung Pay and Google Pay. Business: SME banking and a Personal Financing Partners Program (S2). API-based banking for fintechs and e-commerce (S7). No investment, brokerage or fund product found on the website (checked 2026-10-12).

D360 publishes no income statement that was found. Derayah reports its equity-accounted share of D360 losses: SAR 57m in 1H 2026 (SAR 62m in 1H 2025) and SAR 28m in 2Q 2026 (S6, p.5-6); Derayah says D360 passed its peak loss phase in 2025 (S7).
No investment product on the website (S2); Derayah materials (S6, S7).

capabilities.wealth_summary: D360 is a Shariah-compliant retail and SME digital bank (3m+ customers, SAR 3.6bn deposits and SAR 500m of loans disbursed at end-June 2026) with no investment, brokerage, fund or wealth product found on its website (checked 12 Oct 2026). Savings are the Sanabil Monthly and Daily accounts (expected variable profit 1.0% to 3.0% by balance band from SAR 1,000, as of 28 Dec 2025). Lending is personal financing (SAR 5,000 to 1,000,000, 3 months to 5 years, APR from 4.49%, Saudi nationals only) and SME finance planned with the 2026 capital raise. The shareholder Derayah Financial (listed brokerage and asset manager with the Derayah Smart robo-advisor) said in Aug 2026 that it is piloting integration between the Derayah platform and D360 so clients can move between investing and banking, and that selected services provided through D360 will extend Derayah's offer. D360 also pitches an API-based banking line to fintechs and e-commerce companies.

opportunities: 3m+ customers and SAR 3.6bn deposits at end-June 2026 with no investment, funds or wealth product on the site; savings limited to Sanabil accounts (S6, S2, S3).
SAR 1.5bn capital raise approved Jun 2026 to expand lending, SME finance and API banking; a Series A with international investors is under way (S12, S13).
Derayah has said it is piloting integration with D360 so clients can move between investing and banking (S6).
barriers: Shareholder Derayah (20.4%, appoints more than 30% of the board per a filing summary) already runs brokerage, funds and the Derayah Smart robo-advisor and plans services through D360, so it is the likely default investing partner (S6, S7, S24).
Shariah-governed bank: any shelf needs Shariah screening and committee approval (S1).
Still in an investment phase: Derayah's share of D360 losses was SAR 57m in 1H 2026; use of new capital is stated as lending, SME and API banking, not wealth (S6, S12).
No wealth, investments or digital-product head named on the official list; CFO status unclear (S1, S13).

discrepancies.detail: Al Arabiya (summarising Derayah's Tadawul filing) and EnterpriseAM give capital rising 38.9% to about SAR 2.92bn on 72.9m new shares at SAR 20.57; Mubasher and Derayah describe a SAR 1.5bn raise at a SAR 4.5bn pre-money valuation without a total-capital figure. The figures do not reconcile cleanly (72.9m shares at SAR 20.57 equals about SAR 1.5bn of proceeds, while a 38.9% rise from SAR 2.1bn implies about SAR 817m of new capital; the nominal share value is not stated in the sources).
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded paid-up capital as SAR 2.1bn (pre-raise, website footer) and gave raise terms in initiatives; the post-raise capital is unconfirmed until D360 or Derayah's Tadawul filing is read.

discrepancies.detail: SAMA's digital banks page lists only STC bank and Saudi Digital Bank, both 'Licensed - has not started yet', and omits D360 Bank, although SAMA gave D360 no-objection to launch in Dec 2024 and the Cabinet licensed it in Feb 2022.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the licence decree on D360's site and the Dec 2024 news; the SAMA page is out of date.

discrepancies.detail: Arab News (Jun 2025) says D360 had over 1 million users; Derayah's chart shows about 1m in May 2025, 2m in Oct 2025 and 3m in Apr 2026; Derayah says 3m+ at end-June 2026; an agency release says 3.4m+ in Sep 2026.
discrepancies.resolution: Consistent growth path; recorded the end-June 2026 figure as the primary value and Sep 2026 as an extra record.

open_items: No D360-published financial statements, Pillar 3 report or annual report found (investor page is a contact form). Total assets, net loans, equity, net loss and employee count are not recorded; deposits, customers and disbursed loans come from shareholder Derayah's 2Q 2026 release. Derayah's FY2025 statements and Tadawul filing (Saudi Exchange, HTTP 403) should be read via a permitted route for D360's associate note.
SAMA's own D360 announcement was not found on sama.gov.sa; the Dec 2024 date comes from Mubasher and Derayah's presentation.
PIF's percentage and other shareholders (including the 2018 founding investors) are not disclosed; the PIF portfolio page returned HTTP 403.

Seven directors on the official board list are not profiled (Nouf AlJoaid, Fahad AlJomaih, Faraz Khalid, Mudassir Sheikha, Tim Brooke, Ibrahim Al Jammaz, Bassem Al Sallom), nor are the Chief Legal, Compliance and Internal Audit heads (Yara AlZouman, Mohammed Al Khomashi, Shihanah Al Yousef) or the other two Shariah Committee members.
CFO: Mohammed Nazer was named CFO in Jun 2025 but is absent from the official management list read on 12 Oct 2026; confirm whether he is still in role.

LinkedIn: CEO profile could not be matched to D360 from search snippets (two same-name candidates); Chief Treasury & Investments, CTO and several others were not matched. No chief digital, product or wealth head is listed.
Whether D360 has launched or plans investment or wealth products, and how the Derayah integration will work, is not stated; check the D360 app and Derayah's 3Q 2026 release (expected Nov 2026).

Intellinews (600,000 customers; AI-powered financing launch) and PIF portfolio page returned HTTP 403 and were not opened; Thunes (2023) and TerraPay partnership details were seen only in search summaries and are not relied on beyond the EnterpriseAM mention.

A 'Saudi Digital Bank' licensed on 22 Jun 2021 (SAR 1.5bn, group led by Abdul Rahman bin Saad Al-Rashed and Sons, per SAMA) is a different licence from D360's decree of 15 Feb 2022; the two should not be conflated (see sa-stcbank source S11).
